title: CAMS2_54b Co-design of GHG policy services in support of EU Member States and Copernicus Participating countries
description:
The successful bidder will propose the interaction with national inventory agencies and related institutes that are responsible for national monitoring of GHG emissions and the reporting to the UNFCCC . 
The successful Tenderer shall carry out the following activities:
•	Detailed familiarisation of the successful Tenderer with the latest status of current and emerging operational CAMS products and the use of satellite Earth Observations (EO) for GHG emissions monitoring. 
•	Facilitate collaboration between European national inventory agencies and CAMS. 
•	Collect, document and analyse user requirements at national level for EU member states and Copernicus participating countries. 
•	Provide recommendations for the development of policy-relevant tools, including data visualisation,  at national level.

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a wideband analogue beamforming integrated circuit (BFIC) capable of covering the entire frequency range from Cto Q/V-band, with two beams. This BFIC will serve as a modular and scalable solution for user-terminal flat-panel arrays, enabling multi-band and multi-product compatibility.Targeted Improvements: - Frequency coverage extended from C-band to Q/V-band in a single BFIC.- Fostering high-volume production scalability and economies of scale.- Enhanced design modularity, enabling flat-panel antennas to scale in aperture size (same number of beams) and/or number of beams (same aperture).Description:Conventionally, different BFICs have been used in applications at different frequency bands, e.g., the C- to Q/V-bands relevant to satcom. Also, such conventional BFICs typically generate a single beam. To enable the use of thesame BFIC in a broad range of satcom products, this activity will develop a next-generation dual-beam analogue BFIC with wideband coverage from C- to Q/V-band. Thus, the envisioned BFIC will serve as a fundamental building block for future flat-panel antenna arrays, supporting scalable designs by allowing additional BFICs to be integrated based on performance requirements. The development of this BFIC shall leverage insights from recent state-of-the-art wideband single-/dual-beam BFICs, such as the C- to Ka-band BFICs, which are developed outside ESA Member States. These contributions highlight the growing industry demand for multi-beam and frequency-agnostic BFIC solutions, which can reduce system complexity and accelerate product development, with the potential for higher volumeproduction in comparison to single-band BFICs. Therefore, the envisioned BFIC will cover the entire C- to Q/V-band range and generatetwo beams, which will enable its reuse across multiple product lines and reduce the need for band-specific BFICs. The design willemphasise performance consistency across the wide frequency range, minimising variations in gain, noise figure, and linearity.Additionally, the activity will assess the thermal and power consumption challenges associated with multi-beam and broadband analogue BFICs at millimetre-wave frequencies, ensuring that the proposed solution is viable for both low- and high-end satcom applications. Successful execution will position Europe as a leader in wideband BFICs, securing our competitiveness in the evolving satcom ecosystem. The wideband analogue BFIC will be tested against DVB-S2/S2X or 5G-NR waveform in a relevant environment.

original.description: As part of the European Resilience from Space - Earth Observation (ERS-EO) Element 2 Programme, and in line with the Space Resilience Node (SRN) Workplan 2026 approved on 26th February 2026, ESA intends to issue a competitive tender (ERS-SRN-02) for one (1) harmonization study (up to 300k, 5 - 12 months) which will consolidate the findings from individual SRN User Needs Studies (see Tender Action 1000046333). The objective of the study is to derive or confirm common user needs and requirements for SRNs to inform the SRN Reference Framework, and to identify gaps in space-enabled products to support SRN users' public protection and disaster response activities.

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop bundle protocol and network stack, enabling automatic high-volume end-to-enddata distribution within integratedRF and optical networks. The testbed shall be developed to test networks feature heterogenous links, e.g. in terms of data rates or latencies, and includeend users, mission and payload control centres, optical and RF ground stations and space data relay systems.TargetedImprovements:Standardised data distribution irrespective of RF or optical communication.Reduced ground segment complexity (single system for RF and optical).Automatic network-based distribution.Increased E2E data delivery accountability leveraging unified reporting.Description: The need for hybrid (optical and RF) networks is due to the volumeof data transferred by satellites 00that is ever increasing. Optical communicationpotentially combined or augmented with RF communication at higher frequencies is supporting high or very high data rates. The distribution of this datais non-trivial and faces several challenges like non-permanent connectivity and asymmetric data rates in space and on ground just to name a few. It ishighly desirable to take a reliable and interoperable end-to-end approach with a common addressing scheme to cross organisational boundaries whilebeing able to monitor and manage the overall process of data distribution.The activity will develop an integrated optical andRF scalable high-volume data distribution testbed (demonstrating beyond 1 TB per downlink) based onDisruption Tolerant Networking (DTN). The activity will develop combined software and hardware. The testbed will be tested for high speed DTN nodesconnected over Wide Area Networks, emulating end users, control centres, and ground stations connecting with simulated spacecraft. It will includemonitoring and control aspects of individual nodes and DTN Network Management. The activity will allow the gathering of valuable experience in arepresentative environment and will address the problem of reliable and efficient data distribution in heterogenous ground networks and prepares theexpected deployment of DTN in space nodes in the future.

original.description: Objective:To develop a portable modem that can be easily integrated in an existing optical ground station to make it compatible with ESTOL specificationsTargeted Improvements:Increased interoperability between existing optical ground stations and future satellite systems (e.g., HydRON).Description:There are a number of existing or planned optical ground stations (OGSs) that are currently used for scientific missions or to demonstrate quantum technologies. Those OGSs are not compliant to the ESA Specifications for Terabit/s Optical Links (ESTOL). To maximise the benefit of early Member State investments, the activity shall develop an upgrade kit" for multiple existing OGS infrastructures. An easy-to-integrate modem will facilitate the upgrade of such existing or planned OGSsand increase their interoperability with future commercial and institutional systems that will adopt ESTOL and its evolutions.Thisactivity shall develop a portable breadboard for an ESTOL-compliant modem. In the scope of the activity, it shall be assumed that thetarget existing OGSs have already been developed in terms of optical elements (e.g., aperture, adaptive optics, etc.) in order tobecompatible with ESTOL. The portable modem shall be connected to the optical part of the OGS by optical fibre, and it shall implement both transmit and receive functionalities. The modem breadboard shall come with a GUI and an interface control document to facilitate its fast and easy integration and use. The functionalities of the portable modem shall be validated in the Contractor's laboratory and in an existing selected OGS.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).
